title: Senior Threat Research Engineer, Security Factory: Threat Research
location: Remote, Israel; Remote, Poland; Remote, United Kingdom
description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As a senior researcher in GitLab's Threat Research group, you'll turn emerging security threats into protection for GitLab customers. You'll lead your own research projects, taking ideas from the first question to a working proof of concept, deploying it, and analyzing the results. You'll also keep the detection systems you build running in production. Artificial intelligence (AI) is central to how we work. We build agentic workflows for research, analysis, and detection, and use AI tools every day to move faster. This is a full-stack research role: you'll combine an adversarial mindset with the software engineering skills to build and operate the systems behind your work. What you’ll do Lead your own research projects, from the first idea to the published result. Research new attack surfaces and threat vectors, including AI coding agents, agent plugins, and package ecosystems. Find and responsibly disclose vulnerabilities in open source projects and developer tools. Analyze supply chain incidents and events. Build AI-powered workflows and agents that automate research, analysis, and detection. Build and maintain the cloud-based systems behind our detection and advisory work. Improve the quality and coverage of our vulnerability and malware advisories. Write up your findings as blog posts and present them at conferences. What you’ll bring Hands-on security experience in research, malware analysis, penetration testing, or security tooling, with published findings such as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) records, responsible disclosures, blog posts, or talks. Experience researching AI agents, large language model (LLM) applications, or Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and using AI in real work through LLM application programming interfaces (APIs) or agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, or agent software development kits (SDKs). The ability to build systems and assess how to break them, with strong Go or Python skills and practices including testing, code review, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), and maintainable code. Experience deploying and running production services on a public cloud. An understanding of package ecosystems and supply chain attacks, informed by current security and AI industry trends. The ability to map attack vectors, explain trade-offs, and use data to move experiments forward while balancing quality, speed, and customer outcomes. Clear writing that explains findings to both engineers and a general audience. Helpful but not required: Google Cloud Platform (GCP) experience, infrastructure as code with Terraform or OpenTofu, databases or data pipelines at scale, and reverse engineering. You don't need deep knowledge of compilers or static application security testing (SAST) engines. A high-level understanding is enough. You don't have to match every listed requirement exactly to be considered. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply. About the team The Threat Research group at GitLab researches security threats as they emerge and turns what we learn into protection for GitLab customers. We maintain the GitLab Advisory Database , which powers GitLab's dependency scanning. We also build detection capabilities, do original vulnerability research, and publish what we find. Recent work includes the Shai-Hulud npm worm and a critical RCE in Serena , a popular MCP coding agent. More on the Security Labs blog .
